context: A briefing for volunteers at the Porthaven Harbour Festival

cues.t: Part 2. You will hear the organiser of a harbour festival giving a briefing to new volunteers. First you have some time to look at questions 11 to 15.
Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 15.

Hello, everyone, and thanks for volunteering at this year's Porthaven Harbour Festival. I'm Beth Carey, the organiser. Visitors will ask you all sorts of questions over the weekend, so I'd like to make sure you've got the answers.

Some of them will want to know how the festival began. Many people suppose it was dreamed up by the tourist office, and others think it was a way of honouring the local fishing fleet. In fact, back in nineteen eighty-two, the lifeboat station urgently needed a new boat, and a few local families held a seafood supper to raise money for it. We still give part of our profits to the lifeboat today.
Since then, it has grown from one evening in a church hall to a weekend that attracts around thirty thousand people.

Now, what's different this year? Entry remains free, and we'll be finishing at ten o'clock on both nights, just as we did last year. The big change is transport. Because the harbour car parks fill up so quickly, there'll be a free shuttle bus from the railway station, running every fifteen minutes.
Please tell visitors that the last bus leaves the harbour at half past ten.

Everyone asks about the boat parade, which takes place at noon on Saturday. We've never had to cancel it, and we won't make it any shorter, because some of the boats travel a long way to be here. If the wind is too strong on Saturday, the parade will simply take place at the same time on Sunday.
The best place to watch it is from the quay, but that gets crowded, so suggest arriving at least half an hour beforehand.

Our chefs will be giving cookery demonstrations on both days. Visitors don't have to pay for these, but there's limited space in the tent, so they need to pick up a free ticket from the information tent on the morning of the demonstration.
Each session lasts for about forty minutes, and the recipes are printed on the back of the programme.

And one last point for visitors. Dogs are welcome, as long as they're on a lead. The seagulls can be a nuisance, I know, but the stallholders will warn people about those. What we really want to do this year is cut down on waste, so please encourage everyone to bring their own reusable cup. The drinks stalls won't be giving out disposable ones.
Before you hear the rest of the briefing, you have some time to look at questions 16 to 20.
Now listen and answer questions 16 to 20.

Now, please look at the site map. The main gate is on Harbour Road, at the north of the site, so as you walk in, you're facing south, towards the sea. A wide path runs straight ahead of you, down to the quay.
The information tent is the first thing you'll come to. As you walk through the gate, it's just inside, on your left. The first aid post is directly opposite.
That tent is where you should report for duty each morning, and collect your radio.
Walk on down the main path. Just before you reach the quay, you'll see the seafood market on your right-hand side, and the craft stalls are straight across the path from it.
When you get to the quay, turn right and follow it as far as you can go. The music stage is at the far western end of the quay, so the sound carries out over the water, and not towards the houses.
Bands will be playing there from two o'clock onwards on both afternoons.

The children's area has been placed well away from the crowds. Go back up the main path a little way, and take the side path heading east, behind the craft stalls. Follow it to the end, and you'll find the children's area on the eastern edge of the site.
There are face painters and a small puppet theatre there, and parents must stay with their children at all times.
And finally, the boat trips. Tickets are sold from a kiosk on the pier. The pier runs out to sea from the eastern end of the quay, and the kiosk is right at the very end of it.
That is the end of Part 2. You now have half a minute to check your answers.
